prior_importants.description: For an `awaiting-review` or `blocked` session, the recorded `tmux_target` is matched against every probed server, whatever its lifetime. tmux pane ids belong to one server instance and restart at `%0`. So a closed window's id often matches an unrelated pane, the rescope is refused, and the operator can't get out of it.

The probe looks tmux up only on `/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, while launches use the operator's PATH. Operators whose tmux is installed elsewhere can never rescope, and the refusal message blames an open window.

findings.description: A rescope that lands while `pup fix` is starting a round on a merged session is lost. That round runs under hooks compiled from the old scope, and `recordSessionRoute` then writes its standard route back over the critical tier the rescope just set.
findings.body:
A rescope that lands while `pup fix` is starting a round is lost. That round runs under the old hooks, and its standard route permanently overwrites the critical tier the rescope set on the session.

`startFixRound` reads the session row once. It then computes the route from that copy's tier and recompiles the profile from the current spec (`readTaskSpec`, old `scopeIn`). All of this happens while the session is still `merged`:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b82e81ed4cde08eeb31b2b158f4ed1f9abe56e22/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L193-L231

The state only leaves `merged` at `takeFixRoundEdge` (L226). Until then `rescopeTask` passes both of its checks:
- Its guarded UPDATE allows `merged` (`RESCOPABLE_STATES`).
- The window probe finds nothing, because the gate already killed the merged session's window.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b82e81ed4cde08eeb31b2b158f4ed1f9abe56e22/src/core/session.repository.ts#L355-L398

So the rescope widens `scopeIn`, and `raiseToCritical` sets both `tasks.tier` and `sessions.tier` to critical:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b82e81ed4cde08eeb31b2b158f4ed1f9abe56e22/src/core/task-rescope.service.ts#L259-L275

The round then opens its window with the profile compiled from the old scope and the standard route, so the worker is still blocked from the paths the operator just added. Once the kickoff lands, `recordSessionRoute` writes the stale route back with no guard (`UPDATE sessions SET tier = @tier, rung = @rung ...`):

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b82e81ed4cde08eeb31b2b158f4ed1f9abe56e22/src/core/fix-round.service.ts#L976
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b82e81ed4cde08eeb31b2b158f4ed1f9abe56e22/src/core/session.repository.ts#L539-L546

Afterwards `sessions.tier` is standard again, while `tasks.tier`, the `rescope` event and the CLI line all say critical. Every later fix round climbs the standard ladder. Rescoping again does not repair it: the globs are already in the spec, so `added` is empty and the raise is skipped (task-rescope.service.ts L249-256). ADR 0115's *Tier* and *What reads it* sections promise that the next round sees both the widened scope and the critical tier, so this breaks the decision's own guarantee.

**Trigger:** the normal split of duties, where the conductor runs `pup fix` and the operator rescopes, often in response to the same CI review. The window runs from the session read at L193, through the gh round-trips and the worktree restore, to the edge at L226.

**Possible fixes:**
- Have `takeFixRoundEdge` re-read the session's tier and the task's spec inside its transaction, and refuse with nothing started if either changed since they were read.
- Or make `recordSessionRoute` never lower a stored critical tier. That fixes the tier half only, not the stale hooks.

findings.description: The new `src/core/task-rescope.test.ts` is colocated, but ADR 0116 §Tests and general.md §File naming put new unit tests at `test/unit/<path>/` with the role's dot hyphenated (`test/unit/core/task-rescope-service.test.ts`). The Ceilings clause only grandfathers existing tests, and vitest already includes `test/**`.

`callerTty` runs `/usr/bin/tty` by absolute path, but NixOS (which this PR adds to `PROBE_PATH`) has no `/usr/bin/tty`. Every NixOS operator rescope therefore records `tty: null`, the shape ADR 0115 *The record* calls the suspicious no-terminal case. Look `tty` up on `PROBE_PATH` like `listPanes`/`listProcesses` do.

`listProcesses` looks `ps` up on `PROBE_PATH`, where the user-owned Homebrew prefixes (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, Intel `/usr/local/bin`) come before `/usr/bin`. A worker or the conductor can plant a `ps` there that prints a clean table and passes `launchedAncestor`. ADR 0115 doesn't list this. A system-only PATH for `ps` (`/usr/bin:/bin:/run/current-system/sw/bin`) closes it.

`defaultSocketIn` joins `TMUX_TMPDIR` without resolving it. A launch from a shell with a relative `TMUX_TMPDIR` records a relative socket that `LAUNCH_SOCKET` rejects, while tmux opens the window under `<cwd>/<dir>`. The probe then never asks that server and can report a live window closed. `resolve(dir || '/tmp')` fixes it.

`rescopeTask`'s JSDoc says a window is open when "a default tmux server lists" it, but the probe also asks every socket a session recorded in `tmux-socket`. A reader of the JSDoc won't expect a non-default socket to block a rescope; say "a tmux server lists, at a default or a recorded socket".

`OpenWindow.kind`, `LaunchedAncestor.kind` and `RescopeCaller.by` are new literal unions. general.md §Code layout and ADR 0116 make a closed set of kinds a `string` enum in the area's `enums/` folder for new code.

`getProject(db, task.project_id)?.repo_path ?? ''` silently falls back to an empty repo path, which would make `windowSockets('')` look for socket records under the wrong directory. Refuse on a missing project instead of carrying a silent `''` branch.

process_issues.description: Skipped: `context` (no spec/protocol/infra surface touched), `spec` (no closing issues or spec source in the body or commits), `workflow-safety` (no `.github/workflows` change), `maintainability` (off the default roster at standard depth). Dropped two minors that missed the finding bar: a low-confidence simplicity nit on the process-tree walk's `seen` Set, which its reviewer called defensible, and a low-confidence docs nit on LOOP.md wording, which the reviewer said was unlikely to mislead.

The conventions finding on the colocated `src/core/task-rescope.test.ts` was raised as important and CONFIRMED. On the validator's advice, the orchestrator downgraded it to nit: there is no behavioral impact, and the ADR 0116 migration is in progress, with every other `src/core` test still colocated.
A security instance's `bash scripts/adr-index.sh` call was refused under the CI lock. It read ADR 0115 and ADR 0047 directly instead.
